query:
Who made the argument that natural Beaujolais wine is currently being overlooked by drinkers in the UK, and what in their phrasing correctly identifies them as the source?

Options:
A. Felix
B. Marcus
C. Kezia
D. Dom
context:
[1] (about=Marcus, episodic, t2 @2025-09-08T19:09:00) Honestly, the thing is, the natural wine people in this country still sleep on Beaujolais. Some of the best skin-contact work in France is happening there right now and everyone's still chasing Burgundy or the trendy Jura stuff. I want to open something from that region on Sunday.
[2] (about=Dom, core, t2 @2025-09-08T19:03:30) Dom increased his training volume this week, legs and conditioning, intense, needs calories Sunday, happy with red wine.
[3] (about=Felix, episodic, t4 @2025-09-15T19:13:00) The Lapierre was a good choice. The lamb and the wine worked well together. The orange from Georgia was less predictable than expected, in a positive sense.
[4] (about=Marcus, core, t2 @2025-09-08T19:03:30) Marcus wants to open a Beaujolais wine on Sunday, noting natural wine people overlook it.
[5] (about=Marcus, core, t2 @2025-09-08T19:03:30) Marcus has the Lapierre, cellar stays cool, also thinking of a Georgian orange wine to start.
[6] (about=GROUP, said_by=Marcus, group-interaction, t2 @2025-09-08T19:03:30) Marcus says wine is sorted, guests can bring flowers if they want but not required.
[7] (about=Zara, episodic, t2 @2025-09-08T19:08:00) Marcus the squash and tomatoes sound literally perfect, I'm so on board with the menu 🌿 what's the wine situation though, this is important
agent_answer:
B. Marcus.

His phrasing — “the natural wine people in this country still sleep on Beaujolais” — identifies him as the source, and the memory slice confirms Marcus wants to open a Beaujolais wine on Sunday, noting natural wine people overlook it.
